display.purpose: The document's H1 in the theme's voice (1.9em, 600).

title.purpose: H3 (1.2em, 600); the outline lists H1 to H3 only. H4 is 1.1em and H5 and H6 are 1em, in the editor and the reading view.

body.purpose: Document text in the theme's voice: 18px by default, any size from 15 to 22 in the web dialog and the desktop Settings window alike, line-height 1.9.

dialog-title.purpose: Dialog headings, in the UI sans (`--font-ui`).

label.purpose: The interface's working size (12px, UI sans, `--font-ui`): buttons, menu items, segmented items, captions, notes. The chrome's base is 13px, its smallest text 11px, keyboard hints 10px.

hour-mark.purpose: The large hour character on each Hours swatch, always the book voice.

season-name.purpose: The theme's name on its Seasons or Studio swatch, in that theme's own voice.

code.purpose: Monospace (`--font-mono`: SF Mono, then Cascadia Code, then Consolas) on the code well: 14px in the editor, 13px in the reading view, 0.84em inline. Every code text reads this one stack.

voice-book.purpose: Iowan Old Style with Songti (`--font-song`); the page voice of eight themes (all six Hours, Mist, Harvest).

voice-clear.purpose: PingFang and the system sans (`--font-hei`); the page voice of Lotus, Moon White, Indigo and all fourteen Studio themes.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Every dialog, the command palette included; the largest, softest floating layer. `--shadow` is the ink in light themes and black in dark ones; the dialog scrim takes it at 25%.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: Menus, the outline popover and the find panel.

shadows.name: image-tools
shadows.purpose: The image toolbar, the alt-text popover, the footnote tooltip and the tooltip.

shadows.name: floating-sidebar
shadows.purpose: The sidebar as a drawer over the page; none when docked.

shadows.name: selected-tile-ring
shadows.purpose: The selected tile of a segmented control, the view switch and the Source toggle, in every theme. A ring, not a shadow.

shadows.name: selected-swatch-ring
shadows.purpose: Second pixel of a selected or hovered theme swatch's ring, in the swatch's own ring colour. A ring, not a shadow.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hover changes instantly; nothing eases on hover.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Compact chrome controls while pressed, with no transition; full-width rows and option cards answer with their hover fill instead.

motion.name: drawer-in
motion.purpose: The sidebar drawer slides in over the page; the docked sidebar does not animate.

motion.name: dialog-in
motion.purpose: Dialogs and their scrim fade in.

motion.name: find-in
motion.purpose: The find panel drops into place.

motion.name: theme-crossfade
motion.purpose: Automatic switch between two themes of the same scheme; large surfaces only; text colour changes at once. Never across light and dark.

motion.name: chrome-fade
motion.purpose: Top-bar actions, sidebar button, format bar and status line in Focus mode.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every transition and animation is removed under prefers-reduced-motion; the crossfade is not started.

narrative.overview:
Liubai is one page to write on. The chrome steps back and the page takes the colour of its theme. There are twenty-five themes in three series. The two designed series make each theme a sheet of paper and a colour of ink under a particular light: six follow the hours of a day (天光, Hours) and five follow the seasons of a year (四时, Seasons). Their papers are pearl grey, white, ivory, charcoal, warm brown, blue-grey, grey-green, lotus pink, olive gold, moon white and deep indigo. The third series, Studio (工作坊), carries fourteen established palettes for people who write code and notes: GitHub, Solarized, Monokai, Nord, One Dark and One Light, Dracula, Catppuccin, Gruvbox and Rosé Pine, some in a light and a dark flavour. Body text is always ink. A theme's mark colour shows as thin lines and small marks, and fills only the few primary buttons.

The system is flat and low-interference, following the product principle of editing first. Surfaces are separated by 1px hairlines and at most one tonal step; only a layer that floats above the page casts an ambient shadow. Nothing is textured, gradient or decorative. Hover is instant. Floating layers enter in under 200ms; the one authored moment is the one-second crossfade when the automatic switch turns one light theme into another, or one dark theme into another, as the hour or the season changes.

Two voices speak on the page, both system fonts: a book voice (Iowan Old Style with Songti) and a clear voice (PingFang, the system sans). Each theme picks one for its page, and the chrome around the page always stays in the UI sans.

Confirmed visual rejections: the stock editor theme packs (GitHub, Solarized, Nord, Dracula) as palettes for Hours or Seasons, whose themes are designed for Liubai; those palettes live in Studio, the series made for them. Stationery costume (ruled paper, handwriting faces). Decorative paper cards and slogans around the editor (removed in 0.1.5 at the user's request).
keyCharacteristics: Twenty-five themes, one role vocabulary: every theme declares the same 22 colour roles and a body voice in `src/themes.css`, and components only read `var(--role)`.

Three series: Hours (by local time, six themes, all in the book voice), Seasons (by solar term, five themes, three in the clear voice) and Studio (fourteen established palettes, picked by hand or as the light or dark theme of Follow System, all in the clear voice).
Flat paper: no texture, no gradient, no theme-specific imagery.
Colour has jobs: ink for text, hairlines for structure, the mark colour for the caret, small marks and the primary buttons, the link colour for links in light themes.
The thirteen dark themes separate surfaces with hairlines and one tonal step, and colour only the current thing.
System fonts only, Lucide icons only, chrome in 11 to 13px UI sans.
Exports and print ignore the theme and stay white paper.

rules.name: The Roles-Not-Hex Rule
rules.body: New UI reads roles (`var(--card)`, `var(--primary)`); theme hex lives only in `src/themes.css`. A surface that works in Paper has to work in all twenty-five themes. A new role is declared in all twenty-five theme blocks or in none.

rules.name: The Jobs Rule
rules.body: Each colour has one job: ink for text, pencil for secondary text, hairlines for structure, the mark colour for the caret, small marks and the primary buttons, the link colour for links. Colour never carries a paragraph, and every fill is flat.

rules.name: The Studio Rule
rules.body: Hours and Seasons are designed for Liubai and never borrow a stock editor palette. Studio is where established palettes belong: each keeps its source's recognisable paper, ink and accent, mapped onto the same roles and held to the same contrast checks as every other theme.

rules.name: The Night Rule
rules.body: In the thirteen dark themes (Lamplight, Ink, Moonlight, Indigo and the nine dark Studio palettes) only the current thing is coloured: the caret, the selection, the block handle under the pointer or focus, and the current find match. Links read as ink with a coloured underline. Code uses the `syntax-*` roles, held at 7:1 or more on the dark paper: muted in Lamplight, Ink, Moonlight and Indigo, the palettes' own brighter hues in Studio. A few older accent uses (the table menu button, footnote references, the toast action) still carry colour at night and are not a pattern to copy.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: A theme speaks in one voice on the page: headings and body share `--font-body`. The six Hours themes all use the book voice, so following the hours never reflows the page; the Seasons themes may differ because they change only four times a year. The chrome never takes a theme's voice.

rules.name: The System Fonts Rule
rules.body: The page and the chrome use only fonts that ship with macOS and Windows. A theme never bundles a font file or names one that needs downloading (the only font files in the app are KaTeX's math faces, used for formulas).

rules.name: The Upright Rule
rules.body: Quotes and callouts are set upright. Chinese faces have no italic, so the browser can only slant Songti or PingFang.

rules.name: The Padding Rule
rules.body: Vertical space around editor lines and block widgets is padding, never margin. CodeMirror measures lines and widgets without their margins, and a margin breaks hover, click and scroll positions.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Stacked surfaces are separated by a 1px `border` line and at most one tonal step, never by a shadow. A selected tile (segmented control, view switch, the Source toggle) takes a 1px inset mark-colour ring in every theme.

rules.name: The Float Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this layer floats above the page": menus, dialogs, toasts, popovers, the find panel, the tooltip, the Exit Focus pill and the floating sidebar. It is soft, `--shadow` (ink in light themes, black in dark ones) at 8 to 22%, and never a hard offset; it always darkens.

rules.name: The Line Rule
rules.body: The mark colour arrives as a line, not a block: the caret, the 2px focus ring, the 2px insertion line, the 1px inset ring of a selected tile, the 2px outline of the current find match, the 2px underline on each Hours swatch and the 5px spine on Seasons and Studio swatches. Link and quote colours follow the same habit: a 3px-offset underline and a 2px rule. Fills are reserved for small marks (a resize handle, a checkbox) and the primary buttons: Quick Note's save and a dialog's submit or primary button. The one destructive button fills with rust.

rules.name: The Same-Scheme Fade Rule
rules.body: Fade only between themes of the same scheme. Text flips colour instantly, so a background still fading between light and dark would leave the text unreadable for a moment.

dos: Do read colour through roles: `var(--card)` for paper, `var(--popover)` for anything that floats or docks beside the page, `var(--foreground)` for ink, `var(--muted-foreground)` for secondary text, `var(--primary)` for marks. Check a new surface in all twenty-five themes, not only Paper.
Do keep text ink and hold any new text pair to 4.5:1 or more; text on the hover fill (`accent`) is not gated by the theme check, so compute it by hand.
Do draw the mark colour as a line or a small mark: 2px weights, the 3px underline offset, a 2px ring, a 1px inset ring for a selected tile.
Do separate stacked surfaces with a 1px `border` hairline and at most one tonal step, and give a shadow only to a layer that floats, from the existing vocabulary.

Do keep hover instant. Fade only through the automatic-switch crossfade (the `theme-fade` class on the root: 1s ease, background colour only) and the Focus-mode chrome (150ms opacity), keep entrances under 200ms, and drop all of them under reduced motion.
Do use Lucide icons at the 1.6 stroke and 12 to 19px, through `src/icons.ts`.
Do set vertical space in the editor as padding.

Do run `scripts/check-themes.mjs` after touching `src/themes.css`, and declare any new role in all twenty-five blocks. It holds contrast (ink 11, pencil 5, link 5.5, mark 4.5, quote 5.5, ink on selection and highlight 5, button text 4.5, destructive 4.5, ring 3 and night syntax 7, all on paper; ring 3 on floating paper too), distinctness in OKLab ΔE×100 (hover fill 4 from paper and floating paper and 1.5 from the well; hairline 7.5; highlight 5 and 3.5 from selection; code well and well 2 from paper; rust 4.5 from the mark), and a shadow darker than paper and floating paper.
donts: Don't write a theme's hex anywhere but `src/themes.css`, or branch component CSS on a theme id. Scheme-wide differences go in the `[data-liubai-scheme=dark]` rules beside the tokens.
Don't colour body text, and don't colour links at night: dark themes keep link text ink and put the colour in the underline.
Don't add a gradient, a texture, ruled paper or a handwriting face; the paper is flat.
Don't dim or blur behind a panel whose job is to change what is behind it. The Appearance dialog has no scrim.
Don't crossfade between a light and a dark theme.
Don't bundle a font or name one that needs downloading, and don't give the chrome a theme's voice.
Don't theme exports or print: they stay white paper and black ink.
Don't reuse the swatch spine on other cards; it marks a Seasons or Studio swatch.
Don't give an Hours or Seasons theme a stock editor palette (GitHub, Solarized, Nord, Dracula and the like); established palettes belong in Studio.
